text:
Position-dependent depth weighting has clear precedents. Dou et al.’s [Dynamic Layer Aggregation (AAAI 2019)](https://arxiv.org/html/1902.05770) learns distinct weights over intermediate layer representations at each sequence position, using either a feed-forward combination or capsule routing. This closely matches the general idea of position-wise depth fusion, although demonstrated on Transformers rather than NextItNet convolutional blocks. [SkipRec (AAAI 2021)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16518) provides recommendation-specific adaptive depth through per-user residual-layer skipping; it differs from position-wise soft aggregation. These precedents limit broad novelty claims about adaptive layer selection, without establishing an identical NextItNet implementation.

NextItNet’s causal convolution pads only the left by (kernel_size−1)×dilation, preserving sequence length and excluding future inputs; the [Microsoft implementation](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html) explicitly implements this. For stride-one stacked convolutions, the receptive-field span is R=1+Σ(kernel_size−1)×dilation, summing every temporal convolution, including both convolutions when a block has two. Residual connections preserve shorter paths without reducing the maximum span. Implementation implications: mask padding-derived activations after blocks, normalize across channels rather than time, and read the final nonpadding position; with left padding, count−1 is incorrect.

Architectural inference: yes, deepest-feature-conditioned gates can retain old-history dependence even when selecting shallow features. For z_t=Σ_l α_l(h_deep,t)h_l,t, old interactions can change α_l through the deepest representation while leaving shallow h_l,t unchanged. Consequently, shallow-heavy weights do not establish a short effective history or historical exclusion. Causality remains intact if every gate input depends only on positions ≤t. A guaranteed historical cutoff requires restricting both the selected features and gate inputs to that window; verify by perturbing interactions outside it.
